atoms.text: This guide configures access for the ClipForge transcoder, which reads raw video from the studio-raw-footage bucket and writes encoded renditions to the studio-renditions bucket. The transcoder runs under an IAM role named ClipForgeTranscodeRole in account 111122223333. Create an identity-based policy and attach it to that role. The first statement allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::studio-raw-footage/incoming/*. The second statement allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::studio-renditions/renditions/*. Do not edit the bucket policy on either bucket, because the grant is carried entirely by the role's attached policy. Because the role and both buckets belong to the same account, S3 evaluates the identity-based policy and allows the request without any resource-based statement. To verify, run a test job and confirm that the renditions/ prefix receives the output files and that a request to read any key outside incoming/ is denied.

This guide configures access for the ClipForge transcoder, which reads raw video from the studio-raw-footage bucket and writes encoded renditions to the studio-renditions bucket. The transcoder runs under an IAM role named ClipForgeTranscodeRole in account 111122223333. Add a statement to the bucket policy of each bucket, naming that role as the Principal. On studio-raw-footage, the statement sets Principal to arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/ClipForgeTranscodeRole and allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::studio-raw-footage/incoming/*. On studio-renditions, the matching statement allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::studio-renditions/renditions/*. Do not attach any S3 permissions to the role itself, because the grant is carried entirely by the bucket policies. Because the role and both buckets belong to the same account, S3 allows the request once a bucket policy statement names the role as Principal. To verify, run a test job and confirm that the renditions/ prefix receives the output files and that a request to read any key outside incoming/ is denied.

This guide grants an OCR pipeline access to a single bucket named invoice-archive-prod. The pipeline, called ScanLift, reads scanned invoice images from the scans/ prefix and writes extracted text files to the text/ prefix. It runs under an IAM role named ScanLiftWorkerRole in account 111122223333. Attach an identity-based policy to the role with an s3:GetObject statement for arn:aws:s3:::invoice-archive-prod/scans/* and an s3:PutObject statement for arn:aws:s3:::invoice-archive-prod/text/*. Add an s3:ListBucket statement on the bucket ARN with an s3:prefix condition of scans/*, so the worker can enumerate pending images. The bucket policy of invoice-archive-prod is left unchanged. Since the role is in the same account as the bucket, no additional resource-based statement is required. After attaching the policy, submit one sample image and confirm that a matching .txt object appears under text/.

This guide grants an OCR pipeline access to a single bucket named invoice-archive-prod. The pipeline, called ScanLift, reads scanned invoice images from the scans/ prefix and writes extracted text files to the text/ prefix. It runs under an IAM role named ScanLiftWorkerRole in account 111122223333. Add statements to the bucket policy of invoice-archive-prod with Principal set to arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/ScanLiftWorkerRole. One statement allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::invoice-archive-prod/scans/*, and another allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::invoice-archive-prod/text/*. A third statement allows s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN with an s3:prefix condition of scans/*, so the worker can enumerate pending images. The role itself carries no S3 permissions in its identity-based policies. Since the role is in the same account as the bucket, a bucket policy statement naming it is sufficient. After saving the policy, submit one sample image and confirm that a matching .txt object appears under text/.

This guide covers access for a nightly thumbnail batch job that uses a long-lived IAM user named thumbgen-batch in account 111122223333. The job, called PixelTrim, reads original photos from the uploads/ prefix of the catalog-images bucket and writes 256-pixel thumbnails to the thumbs/ prefix of the same bucket. Create an identity-based policy and attach it directly to the thumbgen-batch user. The policy allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::catalog-images/uploads/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::catalog-images/thumbs/*. Do not modify the bucket policy of catalog-images. Generate an access key for the user and store it in the job's secret configuration file. The user and the bucket are in the same account, so the attached policy alone is enough for S3 to authorize each call. Run the job once and check that every object in uploads/ has a counterpart in thumbs/.

This guide covers access for a nightly thumbnail batch job that uses a long-lived IAM user named thumbgen-batch in account 111122223333. The job, called PixelTrim, reads original photos from the uploads/ prefix of the catalog-images bucket and writes 256-pixel thumbnails to the thumbs/ prefix of the same bucket. Edit the bucket policy of catalog-images and add a statement whose Principal is arn:aws:iam::111122223333:user/thumbgen-batch. The statement allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::catalog-images/uploads/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::catalog-images/thumbs/*. Do not attach any S3 policy to the user. Generate an access key for the user and store it in the job's secret configuration file. The user and the bucket are in the same account, so the bucket policy statement alone is enough for S3 to authorize each call. Run the job once and check that every object in uploads/ has a counterpart in thumbs/.

This guide sets up access for an audio transcription service, VoxLine, which reads recordings from the call-audio-intake bucket and writes transcript files to the same bucket under transcripts/. The service assumes an IAM role named VoxLineProcessorRole in account 111122223333. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::call-audio-intake/audio/*. Add a second statement that allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::call-audio-intake/transcripts/*, with a Condition requiring s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption to equal AES256. The bucket policy is not changed. Configure VoxLine to send the server-side encryption header on every upload; otherwise the write is denied. Same-account evaluation means the role's policy is the only grant involved. Upload a short test recording and confirm that the resulting transcript object reports AES256 encryption.

This guide sets up access for an audio transcription service, VoxLine, which reads recordings from the call-audio-intake bucket and writes transcript files to the same bucket under transcripts/. The service assumes an IAM role named VoxLineProcessorRole in account 111122223333. In the bucket policy, add a statement with Principal arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/VoxLineProcessorRole that allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::call-audio-intake/audio/*. Add a second statement for the same Principal that allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::call-audio-intake/transcripts/*, with a Condition requiring s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption to equal AES256. The role has no S3 permissions of its own. Configure VoxLine to send the server-side encryption header on every upload; otherwise the write is denied. Same-account evaluation means the bucket policy is the only grant involved. Upload a short test recording and confirm that the resulting transcript object reports AES256 encryption.

This guide grants a document conversion service, PageMorph, access to two buckets: docs-intake, which holds uploaded word-processing files, and docs-converted, which receives the PDF output. PageMorph runs under an IAM role named PageMorphConvertRole in account 111122223333. Create one identity-based policy and attach it to that role. The policy allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::docs-intake/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::docs-converted/*. Leave the bucket policies on docs-intake and docs-converted as they are. The output bucket should not be readable by the role, so the policy contains no s3:GetObject statement for docs-converted. Since all three resources are in one account, the role's attached policy is sufficient. Convert a sample file and confirm that a PDF with the same base name appears in docs-converted.

This guide grants a document conversion service, PageMorph, access to two buckets: docs-intake, which holds uploaded word-processing files, and docs-converted, which receives the PDF output. PageMorph runs under an IAM role named PageMorphConvertRole in account 111122223333. Edit the bucket policies of both buckets, naming that role as the Principal. The docs-intake policy allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::docs-intake/*, and the docs-converted policy allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::docs-converted/*. The Principal in each statement is arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/PageMorphConvertRole. The output bucket should not be readable by the role, so the docs-converted policy contains no s3:GetObject statement. Since all three resources are in one account, a bucket policy naming the role is sufficient. Convert a sample file and confirm that a PDF with the same base name appears in docs-converted.

This guide configures a watermarking service, MarkPress, to stamp images stored under a single prefix of the brand-assets bucket. MarkPress reads files from the originals/ prefix and writes watermarked copies to the stamped/ prefix. It uses an IAM role named MarkPressRole in account 111122223333. The role's identity-based policy contains an s3:ListBucket statement on arn:aws:s3:::brand-assets with a Condition limiting s3:prefix to originals/*. It also contains s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::brand-assets/originals/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::brand-assets/stamped/*. The bucket policy is not touched. Without the prefix condition on listing, the role could enumerate keys in other folders, so verify the condition is present before deployment. Test by listing the bucket root with the role's credentials, which should return an access denied error.

The bucket policy contains a statement with Principal arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/MarkPressRole that allows s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::brand-assets with a Condition limiting s3:prefix to originals/*. It also contains statements allowing s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::brand-assets/originals/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::brand-assets/stamped/*. The role has no S3 policy attached. Without the prefix condition on listing, the role could enumerate keys in other folders, so verify the condition is present before deployment. Test by listing the bucket root with the role's credentials, which should return an access denied error.

This guide covers a scheduled cleanup-and-process job, ReelSweep, which reads finished video segments from the segments-staging bucket, writes merged files to the segments-final bucket, and deletes each staged segment after a successful merge. The job runs as an IAM user named reelsweep-cron in account 111122223333. Attach an identity-based policy to that user with three statements. The first allows s3:GetObject and s3:DeleteObject on arn:aws:s3:::segments-staging/*. The second allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::segments-final/*. The third allows s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::segments-staging. No bucket policy is added or changed on either bucket. Enable versioning on segments-staging if deleted segments must be recoverable. Run the job against a test segment and confirm the merged file exists in segments-final and the staged object is gone.

This guide covers a scheduled cleanup-and-process job, ReelSweep, which reads finished video segments from the segments-staging bucket, writes merged files to the segments-final bucket, and deletes each staged segment after a successful merge. The job runs as an IAM user named reelsweep-cron in account 111122223333. Add statements to the bucket policies with Principal arn:aws:iam::111122223333:user/reelsweep-cron. The segments-staging policy allows s3:GetObject and s3:DeleteObject on arn:aws:s3:::segments-staging/* and s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::segments-staging. The segments-final policy allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::segments-final/*. No S3 policy is attached to the user. Enable versioning on segments-staging if deleted segments must be recoverable. Run the job against a test segment and confirm the merged file exists in segments-final and the staged object is gone.

This guide configures a large-file packaging service, BundleMill, that reads multi-gigabyte master video files from the masters-store bucket and writes packaged streaming bundles to the packages/ prefix of the same bucket using multipart uploads. BundleMill uses an IAM role named BundleMillRole in account 111122223333. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::masters-store/masters/*. The policy also allows s3:PutObject, s3:AbortMultipartUpload, and s3:ListMultipartUploadParts on arn:aws:s3:::masters-store/packages/*. A separate statement allows s3:ListBucketMultipartUploads on arn:aws:s3:::masters-store. The bucket policy remains unchanged. Configure the service to abort incomplete uploads on failure to avoid orphaned parts. Run a packaging job on a large master file and confirm that the bundle appears under packages/ with no incomplete uploads listed.
